clips.text: [warm and confident] A user reports a bug. An agent spends real time and tokens figuring it out. It ships a fix. Then the session ends, and what it learned is gone. When the bug comes back, we pay to learn it all over again.

Instead, make every investigation leave something behind. Turn the report into a test that fails for the right reason. Fix the code until that same test passes. Then keep it. Now when the bug comes back, it hits the test, not the user.

Run three of these loops. Replay real failures from user reports. Stress the moments where working features break: restarts, retries, and upgrades. And check the experience itself, on the build people actually install.

Start small: a two week pilot. Five candidate problems. Three lasting proofs. One owner, and a spending limit we agree on up front. On day fourteen, we keep going only if the proofs paid for themselves.
[warm] Spend tokens once. Keep the protection.
